newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Reshuffle on hold as Russia takes holiday.
newsitem.headline: Reshuffle on hold as Russia takes holiday.

text.p: The Kremlin was silent on Monday's Russian public holiday about a government reshuffle, which is expected to follow Friday's appointment of presidential chief-of-staff Anatoly Chubais as first deputy prime minister.
"We have no information," a Kremlin spokesman said when asked whether any announcement might be made on Monday.
He declined to say whether President Boris Yeltsin was at his desk. Eyewitnesses noted that the presidential standard was flying from the Kremlin -- usually a sign that the head of state is present.

Yeltsin appointed his liberal aide and ally Chubais as first deputy prime minister late on Friday. Another Yeltsin decree relieved Chubais of his current job as head of the Kremlin administration. There was no announcement of a replacement.

Kremlin sources said last week Chubais was likely to take the number two post to Prime Minister Viktor Chernomyrdin and that three current first deputy prime ministers would be removed or demoted to deputy prime minister rank.
The appointment of Chubais to the post of first deputy prime mimister in charge of economic reforms had been widely expected.

On Thursday Yeltsin marked his return to the helm of power after eight months of illness with a strong state of the nation speech to parliament in which he promised to streamline the government, bring order and root out top-level corruption.
Chubais, 41, is respected in the West as a dedicated reformer. He is also an excellent administrator and organiser.
But the communist-dominated opposition loathe him for his role in Yeltsin's re-election campaign last year and also accuse him of selling off Russia's state-owned firms cheaply during privatisation.
